findings.title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in list rendering
findings.body: In the `rules.map(...)` loop the `grafana` branch renders `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} .../>` without passing `key={key}`, while all other branches do. React will emit a key warning and, more importantly, lose element identity across incremental page loads of the infinite-scroll list, which can cause incorrect re-use/re-ordering of rule rows and lost component state. Pass `key={key}` as before.

findings.title: Delete and Pause actions silently disappear in the new rule list view
findings.body: Abilities are now also derived from `promRule` (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), so `canDelete`/`canPause` can be true when only a Prometheus rule is available. However the Delete menu item is still gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` and the Pause item on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. Since the list view no longer fetches ruler rules (GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule`), Delete and Pause are never rendered there — a functional regression versus the previous GrafanaRuleLoader which supplied `rulerRule`. Either keep fetching the ruler rule for these actions or implement prom-rule-based variants.

findings.title: Silence menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is provided
findings.body: `canSilence` in AlertRuleMenu can now be satisfied via the Grafana prom-rule abilities, so the "Silence notifications" item is rendered in the new list view. Clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`, but the drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, i.e. when a ruler rule exists. In the list view `rule` is undefined, so the user clicks Silence and nothing happens.

findings.title: Federated rule-group check dropped, allowing edit/delete of federated rules
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`; it now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `isFederated` is hard-coded to `false`. Federated (Mimir cross-tenant) rule groups were intentionally treated as immutable; with this change Update/Delete/Pause abilities are reported as supported for them, exposing edit/delete UI for rules that cannot be modified.

findings.title: View link no longer carries returnTo parameter
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` built the href with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops `returnTo`, so navigating back from the rule detail view loses the user's previous list position/filters.

findings.title: Removed coverage for Creating/Deleting rule operation states without replacement
findings.body: The tests for "ruler-only rule shows Creating state", "prom-only rule shows Deleting state" and the whole `matchRules` suite were deleted. `GrafanaRuleListItem` still accepts an `operation` prop and `RuleOperation.Creating/Deleting` still exist, but nothing now exercises or verifies the eventual-consistency UI behaviour, so regressions there will go unnoticed.

findings.title: Rule-type check placed in the 'allowed' slot of the Silence ability
findings.body: `[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` puts `isAlertingRule` (a support condition, not a permission) into the 'allowed' position. Callers that only inspect `supported` (e.g. to decide whether to render a disabled control) will treat recording rules as silenceable. Move `isAlertingRule` into the supported flag to match the ruler-based implementation semantics.

findings.title: Stale comment/variable name after removing ruler prefetch
findings.body: The ruler `prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup')` dispatch was removed, but the surrounding comment still says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules..." and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`. This is misleading for future readers since no ruler data is preloaded anymore.
